title: Remote and Hybrid Working Policy

headings.text: VI. Health, safety and data protection

key_sentences: This policy explains when employees may work away from an Association office and what both sides can expect when they do.
The policy applies to all employees, including those on fixed-term contracts.
The Association provides the equipment that employees need to work safely at home.
The Director of People will review this policy every two years, or sooner if the law changes.
Employees and the recognised trade union will be consulted on any significant change.

rows: The office named in the employee’s contract, where they work when not working remotely.
An employee who regularly divides their working week between home and their base location.
An employee whose contract names their home as their place of work.
10:00 to 15:00, Monday to Friday, when all employees should be available.
Remains Association property and must be returned on leaving.
Delivered and collected by the IT service desk.
A flat allowance of £18 per month is paid to remote workers only.

list_items.text: 4.1 Any employee who has completed their probation period may ask to become a hybrid worker.
4.2 A manager will normally agree a request unless:
(a) the role requires the employee to be on site, for example:
(b) the employee’s home does not offer a safe and private place to work; or
(c) the team would be unable to provide the agreed level of service to residents.
4.3 A decision must be given in writing within 28 days of the request.
4.4 An employee whose request is refused may appeal to the Director of People within 14 days.
complete the online workstation assessment within their first month of hybrid working;
keep residents’ personal information out of sight of other members of the household;
lock their laptop whenever they leave it, even briefly;
report any accident or near miss through the usual incident form.
